claims.text: An active-learning ML interatomic potential can accurately reproduce solid and liquid free energies across melting.
Active learning can systematically sample extreme anharmonic and electron–vibration-coupling events.
The proposed MLIP can reduce computational cost significantly relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The target systems include elemental Al, elemental Cu, and binary Cu–Ni in solid and molten states near melting.
The training dataset will span harmonic through strongly anharmonic regimes.
The training dataset will include explicit electron–vibration-coupling effects.
A dynamic active-learning protocol will identify and add rare-event configurations to improve coverage of the free-energy landscape.
The proposed MLIP will reproduce the vibrational density of states in both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed MLIP will capture local anharmonic displacements in both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed MLIP will capture electron–vibration interactions in both solid and liquid phases.
Coverage of rare extreme configurations will allow the MLIP to produce statistically converged free energies with the necessary vibrational and anharmonic corrections.
Rapid MLIP evaluation of the free-energy landscape can replace lengthy ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories.
The method will lower computational cost by roughly one order of magnitude relative to both explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The method will maintain phase free-energy differences within 5–10 meV/atom of the reference.
The method will maintain latent heat and entropy-jump predictions within experimental tolerances.
The proposed applicability domain is elemental and binary metallic systems from 0.8 T_m to 1.1 T_m.
Extension to multicomponent systems or more extreme anharmonic conditions is uncertain.
Active learning is expected to mitigate MLIP extrapolation failures for extreme anharmonic displacements and intense electron–vibration interactions.
Deviation exceeding 10 meV/atom in phase free energies or 10% in latent heat or entropy jump relative to a reference will falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to reproduce critical anharmonic features in the vibrational density of states will falsify the hypothesis.
